subject: CanyonPay — Failover audit & deliverables for DR run
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@canyonpay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: CanyonPay Security Team <security@canyonpay.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood — Request: recent DR run evidence and RTO/RPO metrics

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG/CAIQ follow-up we need evidence of Redwood's most recent DR/failover exercise and the concrete RTO/RPO measurements you observed. Specifically we'd like: 
- Executive summary of the failover (what failed, failover path, duration)
- Measured RTO and RPO, and how they were calculated
- Logs or artifacts that substantiate the times (timestamped orchestration events, restore logs)
- Snapshot/backup manifests used for recovery and retention policy
- Any playbook excerpt that shows the automated/manual steps for failover

I'm attaching our questionnaire (CanyonPay_BCP_Questions_2026.pdf) with a few optional items. Our security team is OK with redaction of internal IPs but we do need timestamps and verification of data integrity.

Goal is to complete this by next Tuesday 2026-07-07 so our risk committee can close the item. Please let me know the scope you can provide and any delivery ETA.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Head of Infrastructure Security
CanyonPay
alex@canyonpay.com
+1 (415) 555-0184

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@canyonpay.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood — Request: recent DR run evidence and RTO/RPO metrics

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide all of the items you requested with the following plan: 
- Package: a one-page executive summary, measured RTO/RPO matrix, sanitized orchestration logs, S3 snapshot manifest (hashes only), and a concise playbook excerpt.
- Recent DR run: we completed a full region failover test on 2026-06-28 (internal run id: DR-2026-06-28-07). Measured RTO for customer-facing inference endpoints: 18 minutes. RPO: ~0 (continuous replication with final checkpoint at T-3s). We'll include methodology.
- Redaction: we'll remove internal IPs and ephemeral hostnames but keep timestamps, request IDs, and hash artifacts for integrity verification.
- Delivery: initial package by EOD Monday 2026-07-06; final attestation (signed SOC2 reference + cover letter) next day if needed.

Before I pull everything, could you confirm if we should also include raw KV-cache warmup timelines and sample latency histograms for the first 30 minutes after failover? That tends to be useful for engineering.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Director — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (212) 555-0133

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Redwood — Request: recent DR run evidence and RTO/RPO metrics

Folks — forwarding a customer evidence request (CanyonPay). Need the artifacts below redacted and packaged. Timeline: deliver to me by EOD Mon 2026-07-06. If you need more time, call it out.

Requested artifacts:
- Executive summary (1 page) for external review
- Measured RTO/RPO matrix (per-endpoint) — CSV
- Orchestration events log (timestamps + event ids) — sanitized
- S3 snapshot manifest with object hashes (no full object content)
- Playbook excerpt (failover path) highlighting manual steps
- KV-cache warmup timeline + sample latency histogram (first 30 minutes)

Marissa: can you pull the DR run artifacts from DR-2026-06-28-07 and confirm the measured RTO/RPO numbers? Ben: I may need your sign-off on redaction approach and SOC2 reference to include.

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood — Request: recent DR run evidence and RTO/RPO metrics

Vanessa —

Pulled artifacts from DR run DR-2026-06-28-07. Quick summary: 
- Scope: simulated regional AZ outage affecting primary US-west cluster with automated routing to US-east warm-standby.
- Trigger to full traffic failover completion: 18 minutes (measured from failover trigger event to 95% of production traffic landing on east cluster). We measured 95% cutover at minute 18; 99% at minute 25 due to background rebalancing.
- RPO: effectively 0 for user-level data. We use continuous WAL replication and durable checkpoints; final consistent checkpoint was T-3s from the trigger.
- Evidence artifacts available:
  * orchestration_events_20260628.log (sanitized, includes timestamps and event IDs)
  * s3_snapshot_manifest_20260628.txt (object keys + sha256 hashes; no object contents)
  * kv_cache_warmup_20260628.csv (samples for first 30 minutes post-failover)
  * rto_rpo_matrix_20260628.csv
  * dr_playbook_excerpt_20260628.txt
  * dr_run_summary_20260628.pdf (one-page exec summary)

Redaction note: logs still contain internal hostnames in a few lines. I propose we replace hostnames/IPs with "[REDACTED-HOST]" consistently and keep all timestamps and request IDs untouched. That preserves correlation while removing network details. Approve?

ETA: I can assemble the customer package and upload to the shared drive by COB Monday 2026-07-06.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood — Request: recent DR run evidence and RTO/RPO metrics

All —

Redaction approach sounds fine to me. Preserve timestamps, event IDs, request IDs, and object hashes. Replace hostnames/IPs with consistent placeholders. I'll attach the SOC2 attestation reference (SOC2 v2025 report) and a short cover letter we can include in the package; that should address their audit team's need for compliance context.

Quick note: include a short paragraph in the executive summary that explains the warm-standby KV-cache behavior and expected latency stabilization window (approx 20–35 minutes). That will help set expectations.

Ben Carter
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
